**VERIFIED 2026-08-24 BY vc ON cc's BUILD AT `7926cfae`, AND THE ROW STAYS `red`.** cc routed the green rather than taking it -- a builder greening their own gate row is the change to stop and route -- so this is the verification, not a re-reading of their claim. The WP three had no door at all before it: `put` has no `Wp` arm, so the address fell to the catch-all, while the thread door refused `wps` BY NAME and sent the caller to that very address. **Two doors pointing at each other and neither opening.** And limb 2 is an **INVARIANT of the verb** rather than a property tested from outside it -- `splice_one_field` re-serialises what it wrote and REFUSES if any key but the addressed one moved -- which is stronger than any external check, because a future field whose serde attributes cause collateral movement makes the verb refuse instead of making a test the only thing standing between that field and a silent clear.

**WHY IT IS STILL RED, AND BOTH REASONS ARE THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN PRINTED OUTPUT RATHER THAN A READING OF THE CODE.** Limb 1: **`AC-08.5: 5 of 11 entity form(s) IN THE POPULATION have no write path through `put`** -- `intent:///issues`, `.../wp`, `.../ac`, `.../wp/01`, `intent:///nodes/ic`. **AND ONE OF THE FIVE IS WRONG, IN EXACTLY THE DIRECTION THIS FILE'S OWN DOC CLAIMS TO HAVE GUARDED.** The sweep drives **`put` ONLY** -- it never calls `set`. `Wp` gained a door and the sweep cannot see it, so **the same file asserts `Wp` has no write path at `:640` and PROVES it has one at `:1218`, and BOTH ARE GREEN**: `every_settable_work_package_field_moves_and_takes_nothing_with_it` drives `facade.set` at `intent:///threads/ST0001/wp/03` and `panic!`s if the set is refused, so its passing IS the proof. **AMENDED SAME DAY, AND THE AMENDMENT LOCATES THE DEFECT RATHER THAN RESTATING IT (ic challenged the wording above; vc drove it and took the correction).** _One of the five is wrong_ is true of the WORKLIST and NOT of the PRINT, and the difference decides where the fix goes. **`:735` prints `have no write path through `put`` -- scoped, accurate, every run.
